For patients older than 12 years, administer 200 mg of cefpodoxime orally every 12 hours for 14 days. Drug Interactions and Precautions: 1. BCG Vaccine (Live): Cefpodoxime reduces the efficacy of the BCG vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Administration of live bacterial vaccines should be delayed until the completion of antibiotic therapy. This combination is contraindicated. 2. Cholera Vaccine: Avoid coadministration of cefpodoxime with the cholera vaccine, as systemic antibiotics may inactivate the vaccine strain. Use an alternative drug or delay vaccination until antibiotic therapy is completed. 3. Microbiota (Oral): Cefpodoxime may reduce the efficacy of oral microbiota products containing bacterial spores. Complete the antibiotic regimen 2–4 days before initiating microbiota therapy. 4. Aluminum Hydroxide: This antacid decreases the absorption of cefpodoxime by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral formulations. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Amikacin: Cefpodoxime increases the nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity of amikacin. Cephalosporins may enhance the nephrotoxic effects of aminoglycosides. Use caution and monitor renal function. 6. Atezolizumab, Avelumab, Balstilimab, Camrelizumab, Cemiplimab, Durvalumab, Nivolumab, Pembrolizumab, Penpulimab, Retifanlimab, Sintilimab, Tislelizumab, Toripalimab: Cefpodoxime may interfere with the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors through an unspecified mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Azithromycin, Clarithromycin, Doxycycline, Minocycline, Tetracycline: These bacteriostatic agents may antagonize the bactericidal effects of cefpodoxime. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Calcium Carbonate, Cimetidine, Esomeprazole, Famotidine, Nizatidine, Omeprazole, Rabeprazole, Sodium Bicarbonate, Sodium Citrate/Citric Acid: These agents increase gastric pH, reducing the absorption and efficacy of cefpodoxime. This interaction applies only to oral formulations. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Digoxin: Cefpodoxime may increase digoxin levels by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral formulations. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Furosemide: Cefpodoxime may increase the nephrotoxicity of furosemide through pharmacodynamic synergy. Monitor renal function closely. 11. Gentamicin, Kanamycin, Neomycin, Streptomycin, Tobramycin: Cefpodoxime increases the nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity of these aminoglycosides. Use caution and monitor renal function. 12. Probenecid: Probenecid increases cefpodoxime levels by competing for renal tubular clearance. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Warfarin: Cefpodoxime may enhance the effects of warfarin through an unspecified mechanism. Use caution and monitor coagulation parameters. 14. Bazedoxifene/Conjugated Estrogens, Dienogest/Estradiol Valerate: Cefpodoxime may reduce the efficacy of these hormones by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral formulations. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but additional contraceptive methods may be advisable. 15. Willow Bark, Rose Hips: Cefpodoxime may increase the levels of these agents by competing for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Monitor closely. 16. Plazomicin: Cefpodoxime increases the nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity of plazomicin. Use caution and monitor renal function. 17. Sodium Picosulfate/Magnesium Oxide/Anhydrous Citric Acid: Cefpodoxime may reduce the efficacy of this combination by altering colonic bacterial flora required for drug activation. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Voclosporin: Co-administration with cefpodoxime may increase the risk of nephrotoxicity. Modify therapy and monitor renal function closely.
